name: Lactation support
summary: Evidence-based, judgment-free feeding help at home or by video.
description: In-home and virtual lactation support in Bend and Central Oregon from a Certified Lactation Counselor (CLC). Visits from $60. Judgment-free feeding help.
intro: As a Certified Lactation Counselor (CLC), I provide evidence-based, compassionate support to help your family meet its feeding goals.

Whether you are preparing during pregnancy, working through the early days, or facing a feeding challenge later on, you will get practical guidance tailored to you. If something is outside my scope, I will connect you with an IBCLC or another provider.

items.title: Prenatal education
items.text: A personal session before your baby arrives: breastfeeding basics, feeding cues, latch and positioning, milk production, pumping, partner support and what to expect in the early days.

items.title: In-home, hands-on support
items.text: We work on latch and positioning, observe and assess a full feeding, do pre- and post-feed weight checks when appropriate, address pain or discomfort and build a feeding plan that fits you.

items.title: Virtual support
items.text: We talk through your concerns, observe a feeding when possible and work on latch, positioning, pumping and milk supply from wherever you are.

items.title: Lactation package
items.text: One virtual prenatal session and two in-home visits, for consistent support through pregnancy and postpartum. More sessions can be added at standard rates.

faqs.q: How is a CLC different from an IBCLC?
faqs.a: Both support feeding families, but training and scope differ. As a CLC I provide education and hands-on help for common concerns. For complex medical situations I refer to an IBCLC or another provider.

faqs.q: When should I schedule a visit?
faqs.a: You do not have to wait until you are struggling. Pregnancy, the first days after birth, returning to work and weaning are all good times.

faqs.q: Do you support formula and combination feeding?
faqs.a: Yes. Every family's feeding journey is different, and you will get the same judgment-free support.
Coverage varies. I can provide a superbill to submit to your insurance.

faqs.q: What is a Certified Lactation Counselor (CLC)?
faqs.a: A trained breastfeeding and infant feeding professional who has completed comprehensive education and demonstrated competency in lactation support, certified through the Academy of Lactation Policy and Practice (ALPP).

faqs.q: Do I need a prenatal lactation consultation?
faqs.a: It is not required, but it can make a real difference. We cover what to expect after birth, normal newborn feeding behavior, hand expression and common challenges, so you feel prepared.

faqs.q: What happens during a lactation visit?
faqs.a: We talk about your goals, review your health and feeding history, observe a feeding when appropriate, answer your questions and make a practical plan.

faqs.q: What should I have ready for my appointment?
faqs.a: If possible, have your baby ready to feed around the time of our visit, and your pump and accessories if you are pumping. No need to clean the house. I am there to support you, not judge your home.
Most lactation consultations last between one and two hours.
Yes. Everything shared during our visits is kept confidential.

faqs.q: What if I need more than one visit?
faqs.a: Many families benefit from follow-up visits as feeding changes over time. We make a plan based on your needs, and more visits can always be scheduled.
